No — that would violate the ticket's explicit constraint, and three failed workarounds is a signal to stop and flag it rather than escalate scope on your own.

The fact that timeout/retry/clock-mock all failed to fully fix it suggests the flakiness isn't in the test itself but in a real race condition in the shared middleware's session-expiry logic — which is exactly the thing you've been told not to touch. That's valuable diagnostic info, but it means this ticket may not be fixable within its own stated boundary.

I'd go back to whoever owns the ticket (or the team owning the shared middleware) with: "here's what I tried, here's why I think the root cause is in the shared auth middleware, and here's evidence" — and let them decide whether to expand scope, assign it to the middleware owners, or accept a narrower mitigation. Modifying shared code used by other services without sign-off risks breaking things well outside this ticket's blast radius, even if your fix is technically correct.

Want help drafting that writeup, or digging further to pin down the exact race condition first so your escalation has concrete evidence?
